Replay

Stormcaller: a Replay-only feature exercise

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Try itWhere the feature livesCompatibilityRecorded implementation constraintsValidation

The Stormcaller is an enemy archetype (kind 6). It closes on a living target, plants its feet, shows its complete danger radius, charges an electrical core and pulses damage around itself. Step outside the ring or kill it during the wind-up. The ordinary no-living-target pause behavior remains shared with the other brains.

Default authored settings: 12 HP, movement speed 65, a 140-unit pulse radius, 45-tick wind-up (0.75 seconds at 60 Hz), 2 damage and 150 ticks between pulses. Spawn grace is 60 ticks. Regular wave runs introduce it from floor 2 where the admitted catalog enables the component. Existing migrated catalogs keep the new component disabled until a new run admits updated definitions.

Try it#

After building the Replay project, run dev/stormcaller.tscn with F6 for a live workbench encounter. It spawns through an admitted development action. Move with WASD, fire with the mouse, and dodge the warning. dev/stormcaller_view.tscn is an independent cosmetic preview of the composed charge view.

For a fixed encounter through the normal game:

Shell
RSY_ROLE=solo RSY_RUN=0 RSY_ENCOUNTER=stormcaller \
  nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/play.sh

Choose Ready/Start in the lobby. This training setup fixes starting positions and holds enemy movement at zero; ordinary waves/workbench use its authored movement. All network participants need matching builds. The recorded feature tests used content-50/J.

Where the feature lives#

Responsibility Source
Inspector attack settings scripts/defs/pulse_def.odin, data/attacks/storm_pulse.tres
Enemy numbers and component reference data/mobs/stormcaller.tres, MobDef.pulse
Immutable baked definition content.Pulse_Def inside the existing mob catalog
Tick-owned charge/cooldown shared/game/pulse.odin, composed from existing saved Telegraph/next_act fields
AI/spawn/wave integration Small hooks in brains/combat/run; any non-prop mob with an enabled PulseDef uses the pulse behavior
Detached display Mob_View carries charge state, fraction and gameplay radius
Authored appearance visuals/enemies/stormcaller.tres reuses existing art with a cyan tint
Local charge animation views/components/charge.tscn and scripts/views/charge.odin
Full-size warning Existing Telegraph child receives the actual radius; Titan's growing warning remains unchanged

The charge component rotates/scales the authored glyph; it cannot deal damage or complete the attack. The reducer owns every transition. Death uses the existing telegraph cancellation/death machinery. Host takeover preserves an already-active charge, matching the existing policy for Titan wind-ups; it does not replay a completed attack. Cooldown/grace remains ordinary saved state.

No transport, rollback, journal or view-pool implementation needed a feature-specific change. No Kit or original-game implementation was changed.

Compatibility#

The Stormcaller addition changed the catalog schema by adding a bounded Pulse_Def to each mob definition. It advanced semantic content from 49/I to 50/J (0x525343524150304a), with network protocol 7 unchanged. Old peers cannot silently share the new contract.

The offline converter accepts content 49 as well as older supported saves. Historical Mob/Catalog shapes are frozen rather than aliasing today's live structs. Conversion fills the new component with zeros, preserving the prior catalog and behavior. It does not add enemies or retrofit new balance settings into an old run. The source-49 checkpoint fixture was captured with the code from before the Stormcaller addition. See save conversion for the existing offline command and identity requirements; write to a new destination. The recording verifier also exposes --content49 for the retained historical model.

Recorded implementation constraints#

The replay/network behavior required ordinary game code and data, with no custom correction or recovery hook. Scene composition worked: an authored child handles charge animation and the existing binding handles entity lifetime.

The recorded compatibility problems came from old archive types referencing the live catalog and tests assuming that adding an epoch was the only schema change. Freezing the historical types and making those assumptions explicit retained byte-preservation checks for every old field.

That exercise led to the authoring tools workflow. Visual registration lives in a typed ScrapEnemyArchetype Resource, and the enemy view has one appearance input. Godot and headless code share a canonical bake instead of separate nested-Resource parsing. The historical catalog has fully frozen type dependencies, and the feature tests use shared correction/takeover and native/WASM/peer helpers. The linked feature receipt below remains the historical record of the original feature implementation.

Validation#

Focused tests cover wind-up timing, warning radius, no repeated pulse, late escape correction, death interruption, mid-charge checkpoint takeover and conversion of the real content-49 checkpoint. Native and executed WASM continuation hashes match. The WASM fixture links normal math through Emscripten and uses sufficient fixed test arena storage for two servers/checkpoints; its memory allocation is a harness choice.

Three actual Godot processes with 120 ms configured latency see the warning, apply one inside hit, preserve the dodging player's HP and agree on the final world hash. The full game compiles for WASM. A separate live workbench check edits PulseDef before admission and verifies later Resource edits cannot mutate the running World. Existing 108 model tests and the older offline save CLI checks pass.

Shell
REPLAY_STORM_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output \
  nix develop --command bash tests/replay_stormcaller/run.sh

Implementation/test evidence records the exact scope and initial harness failures. This does not claim new public server deployment, full browser gameplay or a complete re-run of every old game gate.
